- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) in recent days, model tends to overreact — decrease forecast slightly to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes — especially after sentiment shifts to positive; apply a 5–10% upward bias to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- Model overestimates mean-reversion paths — if recent history shows strong trend, forecast should not revert too quickly; extend trend bias for 3–7 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture early breakout momentum — if sentiment is positive and price rises >5% from 10-day average, adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for next 5 days.  
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and price is trending, model underestimates continuation — add 1–3% bias toward trend direction for next 7 days.  
- Model exhibits “lag” in response to sentiment — if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, forecast should adjust 2–3 days later — delay correction by 1–2 days.  
- Overshoot after spikes: if model forecasts peak then declines, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to average out — use median of recent 3–5 day sentiment to adjust forecast direction.
